title: Reform debated in Parliament
documented_fact: The National Art Collections Bill debates reconstruct the institutional position of the National Gallery and Tate immediately before post-war statutory reform.
why_it_matters: This provides contemporaneous evidence for why governance reform was being considered, rather than a retrospective institutional narrative.
limit_or_continuity: The later 1992 Act supersedes the earlier statutory machinery but not the historical evidence of the reform debate.

title: Modern statutory settlement
documented_fact: The Museums and Galleries Act 1992 establishes the modern Tate Board/functions and its legal relationship with the National Gallery.
why_it_matters: The reciprocal trustee relationship is a statutory/governance fact, not merely an institutional custom.
limit_or_continuity: Tate and National Gallery remain separately governed bodies.

title: Current sponsor framework
documented_fact: The current DCMS framework spells out appointments, accountability and spending controls.
why_it_matters: It makes contemporary administrative leverage visible while remaining subordinate to statute.
limit_or_continuity: The 1992 Act remains the constitutive baseline.
